commentary_segments.text_raw:
Bootstrapping has actually
been introduced to nullify
the effect of the input
capacitance of a coax cable
in front of a preamplifier.
Indeed the second buffer
A2 will ensure that the outer
screen of the coax cable is
at the same potential as the
inner conductor. As a result
there is no voltage difference
between inner and outer
wire of that cable. Its capaci-
tance (of up to 1pF/cm) is
thus nullified. The capaci-
tance of the cable is ‘‘boot-
strapped out’’.
The input capacitance is either quite small or the input impedance is exceedingly high!
